references.text: Sarai gives her maidservant Hagar to Abram as a wife, a parallel action to what Rachel does with Bilhah.
Laban gives his maidservant Bilhah to his daughter Rachel, and it is this Bilhah that Rachel now gives to Jacob as a wife.
Rachel suggests that Jacob should go in to her maidservant Bilhah, so that Rachel can have children through her.
Leah gives her maidservant Zilpah to Jacob as a wife, a direct parallel to what Rachel does with Bilhah.
Bilhah is mentioned as one of Jacob's wives, showing the consequences of her being given to him as a wife.
Highlights the recurring motif of children born through slave women to resolve childlessness.
The direct parallel: the giving of Zilpah to Leah is compared with Bilhah to Rachel.
Strengthens the theme of competing surrogate mothers in Jacob's family.
Confirms Bilhah's identity and her offspring as part of the tribes of Israel.
